description:
## Why

Until `"""` lexed, a `@doc` could hold one line. The library's documentation was a set of labels -- "Maps a function over a list.", "The value for key, or nil." -- which name a function without teaching it. Elixir's own docs are the standard to reach for: a summary sentence, the paragraphs a reader needs, then examples.

Now that `@doc """ ... """` and `@moduledoc """ ... """` carry multi-paragraph text, the library can say what it does.

## Shape

A summary sentence in the present tense describing the return value, any paragraphs that earn their place, then `## Examples`.

**No `iex>` prompts.** fz has no REPL, so a transcript would be fiction. Examples use Elixir's non-doctest form: the call on an indented line, `#=>` and the value beneath.

**Every example is run before it is written.** The value is copied from `fz2 interp`, never predicted and never lifted from Elixir's docs. An example that cannot be made to work is a finding, not something to quietly drop.

Six modules have no `@moduledoc` at all -- `Enum` among them -- and roughly half the public functions have no `@doc`. Those are the gap.

## Constraints

Documentation only: no code, no `@spec`, no clause reordering. The `#` body comments were cleaned separately and stay as they are.

Where fz is narrower than Elixir, say so rather than inheriting Elixir's promise: `Enum`'s second half is typed to lists and rejects a range at compile time, a grapheme is a codepoint, `Map` is a sorted array, `Keyword` has no lazy variants, and there is no `Stream`.

## Note

Nothing executes these examples afterwards; that ratchet is fz-5xp.89.

comments.text: Done in 4d5285826. ~250 functions across 16 modules; 6 new moduledocs. Every example verified through fz2 interp. Gate green: lib 1978/0, matrix 642/0, aot 30/0, cli 225/0, doc, clippy, fmt. 13 diagnostics goldens re-blessed for line drift (stdout identical, diagnostics identical with digits stripped and gutters normalised). Findings filed along the way: .90 atom map ordering, .91 empty-pattern parity, .92 library warnings, .93 unreachable slice, .94 encode! keys, .95 Enum.sort ICE, .96 silent doc interpolation.

title: Give the runtime library Elixir-shaped documentation now that heredocs carry it
